correctness.rationale: The complete proof gives q singleton lower bound and the first-period witness, treats m=1 separately, and exhaustively examines factors shorter than a period versus long factors whose occurrence intervals overlap. A standalone literal-factor enumeration checked 52,430 distinct q-selections across 88 parameter cases; no infinite inference is based on finite data.

originality.rationale: Six actual semantic searches of published research records and primary literature comparisons distinguish the higher-alphabet, partial-prefix all-optimum classification from the already published alternating binary complete-period case. The latter is explicitly conceded; foundational attractor definitions, suffix-tree reductions, infinite-word complexity measures, and morphic fixed-point census do not imply the asserted individual forbidden-choice pattern or its q,r,m count. Residual risk of an implicit specialization remains and independent novelty validation has not been performed.

value.rationale: Exact counting of all optimum attractors, not merely their minimum size, is a natural structural quantity for factor-covering compression certificates. The all-prefix theorem reveals a sharp disappearance of boundary obstructions at r=q-1 and proves one short boundary factor is an iff-certificate for every failure among exponentially many optimal-size selections. It generalizes beyond the known binary full-period census to every alphabet and every proper prefix length.
